newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium to strengthen by fourth quarter - Wolff.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium to strengthen by fourth quarter - Wolff.

text.p: The current climate of strengthening global economic activity should see aluminium prices pick up after the seasonal summer slowdown, brokers Rudolf Wolff and Co said in a special report.
They expect this to happen once fund and technical selling has been absorbed by the market.
A market supply deficit and stocks falling towards critical levels should ensure firmer prices to be sustained through 1998, Wolff said.
Wolff said that aluminium prices were lagging behind the growth in OECD GDP, and with the GDP forecast to expand further into 1998 aluminium has the potential to strike higher.
Should stocks continue to decline at their current rate, commercial stocks will end 1997 at around 5.6 weeks consumption. Traditionally 5.5 weeks is a critical level, Wolff said.
But Wolff pointed out that the decline in stocks cannot be purely attributed to real consumption and re-stocking, as some metal coming out of LME warehouses has been put into financing deals.

These off-market inventories could be between half a million and one million tonnes and although many believe that they will make their way back into the market, the nature of the deals may ensure a lot of the metal is likely to be tied-up until demand narrows the contango and the metal is taken by consumers.

Idle capacity is unlikely to be restarted until stocks have fallen to more comfortable levels or as Reynolds, Alcoa and Alcan, who control 60 percent of the spare capacity, have said, until market conditions dictate, Wolff said.
